rationale: final_mean is lambda-invariant (propagation only reorders visits within an already-reachable set). K's marginal slope (d(final_mean)/dK) drops to <10% of its steepest early value by K=5 (Mirai) / K=10 (Gafgyt); we take the larger, K=10, as the shared choice. At K=10, Mirai captures 97.5% and Gafgyt 86.5% of their respective grid-best final counts. lambda's marginal slope (on AUC, since lambda only affects speed) drops the same way by lambda=1.5 (Mirai) / lambda=2.0 (Gafgyt); taking the larger gives lambda=2.0.
